### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `environmentId (44 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7b25f5ff8251e6b82f481f8e9fefbe0fee01b52a` — the merge of head `f364cc0df846de3bc9d022aae8acd66305fac411` into base `ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7b25f5ff8251e6b82f481f8e9fefbe0fee01b52a && git checkout 7b25f5ff8251e6b82f481f8e9fefbe0fee01b52a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182 f364cc0df846de3bc9d022aae8acd66305fac411 && git checkout -B drift-repro ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182 && git merge --no-ff f364cc0df846de3bc9d022aae8acd66305fac411

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9c404cd8f08f51c63a70561d35812e2b20cda61f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts + packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/index.ts

Inputs read: card #34386 (body and all 6 comments), PR #34492 (body, 9 files, 3 comments), the net diff against the merge base `24b6ae55`, and the check-runs on the head: 72 runs, 60 success, 12 skipped, none failed, none pending. The rest of the diff (the test file, the two docs pages, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `@objectstack/runtime` gains the export `dispatchActionResume` and the type `ActionResumeRequest` (`index.ts`). Additive; no existing export changes. Right.
- `HttpDispatcher` gains the public method `resumeHostActionRun`, a one-line delegate shaped as `dispatchHostAction`. Additive. Right.
- `resumeActionRun` gains the optional `wiring.hostDoor`. Absent, every branch reads as on `main`: `elicitConfirmation` is taken from the wiring, `resumeAdmissionRefusal` gets no fifth argument and asks `aiDoorConfirmation`, the row carries `surface: 'mcp'`. The MCP `resume_run` accept-set is unchanged. Right.
- `resumeDoorError` now also files the envelope in a `WeakMap`. The thrown value and its members are unchanged, so the MCP tool reads what it read. Right.
- `actionDeclarationReads` is `buildMcpBridge`'s own reads moved out; the closures and their order of use are the same, and `readServedObject` stays in the bridge. No accept-set change. Right.
- `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`: docblock text only on `IActionConfirmationService`. No type, constant or schema moves, and no generated artefact is owed (Spec property liveness: success).
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: a new call is accepted, nothing an existing caller sends is refused. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author writes changes.
- System-context register row 52 naming `resumeActionRunRequest` is right: the door opens with the same `shouldDenyAnonymous` read `dispatchActionRequest` opens with, and a system context passes it (then fails step 2, having no `userId`).

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening)

The changeset is `@objectstack/runtime` patch. AGENTS.md rule 3: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The level matches what the diff publishes. `@objectstack/spec` publishes a docblock change only and moves with the fixed group. The two declaration lines are in the PR body and in the changeset body. Check Changeset: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation, `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` outside the first claim: answered. The surface was amended on the card (comment 6932607150), and the row is the census gate's own output for a real anonymous-deny read.
- Dev deviation, PR body r2 sent by the seat: answered; the body on the PR carries the naming, register and verification sections.
- Open question 1 (needs contract review): answered by this record.
- Open question 2 (placement route path `/mcp/resume_run/RUN_ID`): option A, keep. The path is informational, each segment is encoded, and no environment hint is derived from it (`placeHostActionRequest`). It names the door whose steps run.
- Escalated, follow-up card owed (see S1): `ActionConfirmationHandOff.run` names the run and the values, not the pause the values were written for. Binding an approval to its screen would widen a ruled contract shape (#33689, #33690), so it is a ruling, not a fix for this PR.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join; the reads are `getRun` by id and the existing subject `get` by id.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts` against rule 4 of `AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_CAPABILITY` and its first consumer (the cloud approve door of cloud PR #4735):

- `dispatchAction(kernel, { ..., posture: 'ai', confirm: true })` for a handed-off `run_action`: holds. The host door passes no `confirmationHandOff`, so under `ai` it asks the member gate `actionConfirmationRefusal` (`action-dispatch.ts`, the branch after line 601), which admits a person on the boolean `true` and refuses an account.
- `dispatchActionResume(...)` resumes the run the hand-off carries, as that person, every `resume_run` gate asked again; a run no longer paused or another person's is refused: holds, read in `resumeActionRun` steps 1 to 6 with `hostDoor` set.

S1 (should-fix) — "the run resumes once" overstates what the seam checks, in the scenario the card is accepted against (a gated wizard). Step 2 refuses a run that has LEFT `paused`. A wizard that the first approval moved to its next screen is still `paused` under the same run id (`run-resume.ts`, the re-pause answers; the `resume_run` docblock says a wizard is walked by calling again). A second call with the same hand-off (a retried approve request, a second pending item the agent created by calling `resume_run` twice, or an item approved after the person advanced the run in the app) passes steps 2 to 5 and submits the first screen's values to the screen the run is parked on now, as the person, on a `confirm: true` given for another screen. Only the engine's screen contract (#4477) stands in the way, and it admits a bag the later screen accepts. The test pins "once" on a single-screen flow that completes. Fix, prose only, on the contract docblock and the same sentence in the `dispatchActionResume` jsdoc: say that the seam refuses a run that is no longer paused, that a run parked on a later screen is still paused and is resumed with the values given, and that deciding a pending item once, and discarding an item whose run has moved on, is the host's. The `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` and changeset sentences should then say the same. The structural fix is the follow-up card named in ③.

Implementing files, against the contract sentence by sentence:

- `domains/mcp.ts`, `resumeActionRunRequest`: anonymous refusal first, then placement through the host action door's own step, then the environment fallbacks, line for line as `dispatchActionRequest`. Agrees.
- `domains/mcp.ts`, step 3 host branch: `hostConfirmation` is always an object at the host door (`{}` when `confirm` is absent), so the member gate always runs there and nothing reaches `aiDoorConfirmation` or a hand-off. An AI service account is refused with `reason: 'service_account'` whatever it carries. Agrees with rules 4 and 6.
- `domains/mcp.ts`, the invocation row: the host context expression is the one `action-dispatch.ts` line 915 uses for a door with no surface. Agrees.
- `domains/mcp.ts`, `resumeDoorAnswerOf`: a door refusal answers the envelope `deps.error` built; anything else goes through `errorFromThrown`. Agrees with the jsdoc.
- `action-dispatch.ts`, `dispatchActionResume` and `ActionResumeRequest`: one dispatcher per kernel from the same registry as `dispatchAction`; the answer type is `ActionDispatchAnswer`. Agrees, apart from S1's sentence.
- `http-dispatcher.ts`, `index.ts`: delegate and export only. Agree.
- What stays the host's (the person's envelope, the ADR-0069 gate, membership, and the rule that only a person's signed-in session decides) is stated in the jsdoc and matches `dispatchAction`'s list. A delegated agent with `confirm: true` passes the member gate here, as at `dispatchAction`; refusing it is the approve door's rule under the contract, and the jsdoc says so.

Nits:

- N1 (nit) — the jsdoc says a declared-gated action is refused `428` without `confirm`. With two flow actions on the same flow and object, one gated and one not, the gated one refuses and the ungated one admits the resume. That is the door's existing first-admitting-candidate rule and such a run could be started ungated; the sentence is slightly broader than the code. Left as an accepted deviation.
- N2 (nit) — `actionConfirmationRefusal`'s "The enforced set" docblock (`action-execution.ts`, outside the diff) still names `dispatchAction` under `ai` as the one door that reads the member for a person. The host resume door now reads it too. Follow-up card.
- N3 (nit) — `ActionResumeRequest.environmentId` says it is placed as `ActionDispatchRequest.environmentId` is; this request carries no `credentialHeaders`, so with no environment named a resolver has nothing else to place the call from. Left as an accepted deviation.

No must-fix. One should-fix, S1, open on this head: it earns a delta review of its fix.
